findings.evidence: In this commit, `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go:172-205` calls `flushEngines()` then proceeds to `unsafeImportAndResetAllEngines()` without holding any `engineInfo.flushLock`. `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go:236-246` shows `flushEngines()` unlocks each engine immediately after `ei.Flush()`. Writers only coordinate via `engineInfo.flushLock` RLock (`pkg/ddl/index.go:2176-2185`, `pkg/ddl/ingest/engine.go:218-222`), so writes can resume while import/reset runs. Local backend reset is destructive (`pkg/lightning/backend/local/engine_mgr.go:412-452` closes+cleans+reopens engine) and `Writer.AppendRows` does not respect the engine import/close mutex (`pkg/lightning/backend/local/engine.go:1250-1280`). Prior to this refactor, flush locks were held across import via deferred unlock in `Flush()` (`pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go@365a722c:172-205`).
findings.fix: Hold each engine’s `flushLock` (write lock) across the entire flush+import+reset critical section (mirroring the pre-refactor behavior), or introduce an explicit “stop writes” barrier so no `Writer.AppendRows` can run while `unsafeImportAndResetAllEngines()` is executing.
findings.impact: Potential data correctness break (missing/inconsistent index entries) or hangs/crashes if quota-triggered imports occur while other backfill workers continue writing into engines being imported/reset.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (f0813a3696): `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go` still unlocks per-engine inside `flushEngines()` and runs import/reset without holding `flushLock`; `pkg/lightning/backend/local/engine.go` `Writer.AppendRows` still doesn’t check engine import/close lock state.
findings.verify: Force mid-job imports by setting a small `@@tidb_ddl_disk_quota` and running ingest add-index with multiple workers; verify the resulting index with `ADMIN CHECK TABLE/INDEX`, and watch for import/reset errors, stalls, or inconsistent row counts.
findings.what: `IngestIfQuotaExceeded` can import+reset engines while writers are concurrently appending, because flush locks are released before `unsafeImportAndResetAllEngines()`. This can race with local backend import/reset and lead to data loss or corruption in add-index ingest.

findings.evidence: `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend_mgr.go:236-241` encodes duplicate-check dirs as `"<jobID>-dup"`, but `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend_mgr.go:243-246` `decodeBackendTag()` still does `strconv.ParseInt(name, 10, 64)`. Cleanup relies on this decode and skips on error (`pkg/ddl/ingest/env.go:133-143`), so `-dup` dirs won’t contribute a jobID and won’t be removed. These `-dup` dirs are created by duplicate-check backends (`pkg/ddl/index.go:2451-2453` uses `ForDuplicateCheck()`, and `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend_mgr.go:100-105` builds `jobSortPath` with `encodeBackendTag(job.ID, b.checkDup)`).
findings.fix: Make `decodeBackendTag()` accept `-dup` (e.g., trim suffix or split on `-` and parse the numeric prefix), or change the directory scheme so the jobID directory name stays numeric (e.g., subdir `dup/`).
findings.impact: Stale `-dup` ingest temp directories can accumulate and consume disk; over time this can exceed quota and make ingest backfill unavailable or slow, plus it will generate cleanup error logs.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (f0813a3696): `encodeBackendTag()` still emits `"%d-dup"` and `decodeBackendTag()` still uses plain `ParseInt`, while `CleanUpTempDir` still skips decode errors.
findings.verify: Create a temp dir named like `<ingestDataDir>/<jobID>-dup` for a finished job and run `CleanUpTempDir`; it should be removed without logging decode errors.
findings.what: `CleanUpTempDir` cannot clean stale duplicate-check sort dirs (`<jobID>-dup`) because `decodeBackendTag` still only parses pure integers.

findings.evidence: `pkg/ddl/ingest/mem_root.go:142-145` makes `MemRoot.RefreshConsumption()` a no-op (previously it updated from backend manager). `pkg/ddl/ingest/engine.go:139-172` calls `RefreshConsumption()` then `CheckConsume(...)` but never `Consume(...)`, so `currUsage` is not advanced by writer allocations. Memory-based config sizing uses `memRoot.CurrentUsage()` too (`pkg/ddl/index.go:2147-2151`, `pkg/ddl/ingest/config.go:153-200`), which will be stale (often 0), allowing multiple backends to each size themselves as if they owned the full quota. Parent behavior updated usage via backend manager (`pkg/ddl/ingest/mem_root.go@365a722c:145-147`).
findings.fix: Restore global memory accounting: either (a) reintroduce a tracker/registry so `RefreshConsumption()` can sum active backends’ `TotalMemoryConsume()` and update `MemRoot` tags, or (b) convert allocations to explicit `Consume/Release(WithTag)` at writer/backend lifecycle points (and release on Close/unregister).
findings.impact: Memory quota enforcement for ingest is effectively disabled, risking TiDB OOM/severe memory pressure during ingest add-index (especially with concurrent jobs/backends), leading to instability or crashes.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (f0813a3696): `MemRoot.RefreshConsumption()` remains TODO no-op and `engineInfo.CreateWriter` still only checks without consuming.
findings.verify: Run multiple concurrent ingest add-index jobs with high concurrency; confirm writer/backend creation is throttled when nearing quota, and observe memory stays bounded (or add unit tests asserting `CheckConsume` fails after simulated consumption).
findings.what: `MemRoot` usage tracking is broken after removing the backend context manager: `RefreshConsumption` no longer updates usage and allocations don’t call `Consume`, so `CheckConsume` gates are ineffective and memory oversubscription becomes likely.

subject: ddl/ingest: remove backend context manager and refactor code (#57770)
summary: Refactors DDL ingest backend lifecycle by removing the shared backend context manager, introducing `BackendCtxBuilder`, reshaping flush/import/checkpoint APIs, and switching disk tracking to per-backend usage trackers; also changes TS handling to set TS before import and adjusts checkpoint watermark advancement.
